chose: sniff magic bytes and ignore the remote content-type when storing a server-copied hero
over: trusting the third-party host's declared Content-Type via isAllowedImageMime
because: a hotlink-protected CDN answers 200 image/jpeg with an HTML refusal page; the declared type is a claim by a party we asked a favour of, not evidence, and storing it would put a document where a photo belongs and later hand a PDS an undecodable blob

chose: route the server-side copy through presignUpload + a self-POSTed form
over: PutObjectCommand straight to S3 with the bucket credentials
because: the presigned POST policy (eq $key, eq $Content-Type, content-length-range) is what enforces the 2MB cap and the key space; a direct put would move enforcement into app code and add a second write door to blob-storage.ts

chose: copy bytes into a fresh Uint8Array before wrapping in a Blob
over: bytes as unknown as BlobPart (the idiom already in recipes-write.db.test.ts)
because: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> is not a BlobPart under TS5.7 lib defs; the double cast hides the question and .buffer is wrong for any subarray an injected fetchBytes might return. A <=2MB memcpy is free

chose: did not run npx coherence verify despite the 11-commit advisory
because: three other agents are editing this working tree in parallel; a whole-tree verify would report their half-landed changes as mine and the result would be unattributable. It belongs to whoever closes the branch

chose: no new invariant for patch e7b8c7a3499fc8d8
over: add an invariant or boundary claim that the change does not require
because: the new write path deliberately creates no new contract: enforcement of key, content-type and the 2MB cap stays in the presigned-POST policy in blob-storage.ts, which is already anchored and which this path reuses rather than bypasses. The one genuinely new claim -- sniffImageMime never returns a mime the bytes are not -- is a pure-function property whose test file (recipes-write.db.test.ts / a recipe-image unit test) is owned by a parallel agent in this same tree, so pinning it from here would collide
